decision: Retain bounded per-log ownership for large verified cached-viewer responsiveness gains, with explicit cold-index, memory and SDK-tail tradeoffs; not a universal SDK speedup.

build_control.method: Matched uv/maturin production wheels, unchanged profile/features/dependencies; control equals previous native; merged source/binary equal final measured prototype.

ownership.lifetime: Registry read guard held for refresh/query; exclusive registry writes create/prune/evict, then atomically downgrade.
ownership.failures: Refresh error immediately drops index; next exclusive registry write prunes invalid slots before eviction. Query errors retain healthy index.
ownership.limits: Same-log operations exclusive; cold creation/rebuild/eviction waits for active readers; queued writers may delay new readers; sampling still scans/parses selected rows.

methodology.viewer: Fresh servers on CPUs 22/23, client on 23; five alternating pairs and reversed confirmation. Four cached independent log paths share verified fixture; fast/cold logs each ten rows.
methodology.overlap: Large request must remain incomplete while server process CPU advances at least two ticks before fast request. HTTP completion marked after JSON read and before validation; deterministic Rust gate independently proves cross-log critical-section progress.
methodology.shutdown: Harness child-local Python SIGINT handler permits Rust graceful return; clean child shutdown required within ten seconds. No production signal change.
methodology.exclusions: Rejected initial invalid-slot capacity variant and preliminary pre-completion-marker/pilot results excluded from qualified totals.
methodology.sdk: Seven workloads, five alternating pairs and reversed confirmation, fresh processes pinned to CPU 23; no builds/tests during measurement.

validated_output.chart_checks: Totals, first/last steps, max_points bound, each returned metric value.
validated_output.sdk_checks: Every hundred-metric physical row/step/field/value; final series/summary and backend counts where applicable.

environment.gc: enabled; collected before each measured batch
environment.io: warm OS page cache; no fsync; final buffer drain included
environment.memory: fresh-process Linux RSS, including native allocations

native_regressions: Independent cached-log progress; controlled old-runtime failure with safe release/join.
Refresh-error invalidation/rebuild without stale rows; action errors retain index.
Invalidated slots pruned before healthy-index eviction.
validation.artifact_atime: Original assertion retained; passing this run does not resolve known external-access interference. Isolation remains blocked.

tradeoffs: Cached small query during large query: 557.05 to 1.76 ms and 562.47 to 2.20 ms. Four independent cached-log batch improves about 1.9x on two server CPUs.
Cold index creation regresses about 2-3%; cold overlap requests still wait roughly 550-570 ms. No cold concurrency gain claimed.
Post-parallel median RSS rises 91.07 to 105.42 MiB and 91.04 to 103.77 MiB; concurrent working sets increase despite unchanged index bound.
SDK NumPy means regress +0.43%/+0.62%; backend p99 worsens 95.448 to 99.756 and 95.888 to 104.754 us. Other SDK differences/tails small or mixed.
No API, schema, dependency, Python/TypeScript changes, Arc lease or background index pool.
